findings.message: The new `in_prod` subquery works out "a live Prod deployment" again from whichever environment is Prod today (`e.is_prod and d.status = 'deployed'`). The repo already stores that fact once, when the deployment is written: `delivery.deployment.released` (migration 0005, set in services.ts:185). Migration 0005 says it exists so that a change to which environment is Prod can't alter what released a proposal. The two rules disagree as soon as Prod moves to another environment. The previous round's finding was also the class "what decides In Prod", and this fix answers it with a second copy of the rule. Fix: `exists (select 1 from delivery.deployment d where d.release_id = p.release_id and d.released and d.voided_at is null)`, and add a board-092 case that re-marks Prod after the deployment.
findings.scenario: CON v2.4.0 is deployed to Prod (released=true) and its proposals go Released. An admin then marks UAT as Prod with upsertEnvironment, which unmarks the old Prod. The board's card drops from "In Prod · v2.4.0" to "Released". The other way round: a release that was only deployed to UAT (released=false) reads "In Prod" once UAT is marked Prod, although no Prod deployment released it.

findings.message: The 092 AC-1 comment still says "`found` was read before, without a lock". This diff now reads `found` with `for update`. The race test's comment (owner-092.test.ts:55, "The sync reads the row before that commits") is out of date the same way: the sync now waits at that read. Update both so the comments describe the code.

The new merge-commit case checks only that `authorsOf` returns undefined. The previous finding also asked for an end-to-end check that a push of such a record keeps the stored owner instead of clearing it. Nothing here drives that path for the file-present, empty-log case. Add a push assertion next to it, or point to an existing test that covers undefined → owner kept.
